note: Court fees are a State subject (Entry 3, State List). The parent Act is the Court Fees Act, 1870. Each row below is the State's own schedule for an ad valorem fee on a plaint in a money suit, read from the Act text cited in that row. Money suits only: declaratory, injunction, partition, possession and multi-relief suits are valued differently. No row is inferred from a secondary calculator. A State not listed here is shown as 'not yet sourced' and no fee is added to the total.

states.act: Court Fees Act, 1870 as amended for Delhi by the Court Fees (Delhi Amendment) Act, 2012 (Act 11 of 2012)
states.section: Schedule I, Article 1; Article 3 for a s.138 NI Act complaint
states.note: Up to ₹50,000: 2% or ₹1,000, whichever is more. ₹50,001 to ₹20,00,000: 3%. Above ₹20,00,000: 4%. Article 3 applies the same scale to a complaint under s.138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, calculated on the value of the instrument.

states.section: Schedule I, Article 1 (substituted by Maharashtra Act 18 of 2002)

states.act: Karnataka Court-fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1958 (Karnataka Act 16 of 1958)
states.section: Schedule I, Article 1 (substituted by Karnataka Act 2 of 1993)
states.note: Progressive 16-slab schedule. The Act text we read states ₹2,47,125 + 1% above ₹80,00,000. One secondary summary says 0.5% for that final slab; we follow the Act text. No statutory maximum is stated in the schedule.

states.act: Tamil Nadu Court-fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1955 (Tamil Nadu Act 14 of 1955)
states.section: Schedule I, Article 1 (substituted by Tamil Nadu Act 6 of 2017, section 11)
states.note: The 2017 amendment substituted Article 1 with a flat 3% of the amount or value of the subject-matter in dispute. No statutory cap is stated in the amendment. The pre-2017 anna-based scale (about 7.5%) is no longer the operative text.

central.note: The unamended central schedule is expressed in annas (6 annas = ₹0.375) and caps the fee at ₹3,000. Most States have replaced it with their own schedule. It is shown for reference and is NOT used as a default for an unsourced State.

consumer.act: Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020, rule 7(2), as substituted by the 2023 amendment
consumer.note: The fee follows the value of the goods or services paid as consideration, not the compensation claimed. Up to ₹5,00,000 the prescribed fee is nil. Filing is through the Consumer Commission or the e-Daakhil portal.
